coverageNote.note: J.M. Smucker operates roughly 20 US manufacturing plants (Jif, Folgers, Smucker, Milk-Bone, etc.). We audited 14 of them as the core sample.

account.networkCountSource: J.M. Smucker FY2025 Form 10-K, Item 2 Properties (fiscal year ended Apr 30, 2025): 20 US manufacturing and processing facilities. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000091419/000009141925000056/sjm-20250430.htm
account.sampleRationale: The 14 audited plants represent Smucker's 20 US manufacturing facilities running the Jif, Folgers, Smucker, and Milk-Bone lines.
account.dossierIntro: J.M. Smucker runs jam, Folgers, Jif peanut butter, and Milk-Bone. We audited 14 of its roughly 20 US manufacturing facilities as the core sample. The Uncrustables plant in Longmont CO is 91.3 acres of frozen sandwich manufacturing. Topeka KS pet food is 140 acres. 6 of the 14 audited sites are rail-served. YardFlow runs the frozen, shelf-stable, and pet food flows on three protocols inside one gate.
surprisingFindings: Uncrustables Longmont CO is 91.3 acres. The plant exists for a single product: frozen PB&J sandwiches.
Topeka KS is 140 acres of pet food production. Milk-Bone and Meow Mix ship from here.
447 dock doors across the 14 audited sites. Smucker runs efficient dock density per SKU.

sites.name: Coffee Roasting - New Orleans LA
sites.dossierExcerpt:
The roster pin (30.034172, -89.911159, ROOFTOP) landed on the north edge of a
large industrial complex. Satellite probes (z16–z19) revealed a massive
single-roof industrial building with attached processing equipment, silos and a
rail spur along the north edge, consistent with a bulk coffee roasting plant,
not an office. Street View (captured Nov 2025) from the south frontage road
confirmed the Folgers/Smucker coffee roasting building, with its tall processing
tower and a continuous chain-link perimeter fence backed by a hedge.

Web research confirms this is the Old Gentilly Rd plant, opened 1960, acquired
by J.M. Smucker with Folgers in 2008, described as the largest bulk coffee
facility of its kind in the world; it shares the New Orleans operation (>700
employees, 300+ products) with the separate Coffee Silo Operations site.

fieldNotes.location: Folgers/J.M. Smucker Old Gentilly Rd coffee roasting plant, New Orleans East. Confirmed via Street View (Nov 2025) showing the large industrial roasting building with processing tower and continuous perimeter fence/hedge, plus web research (largest bulk coffee facility of its kind in the world; opened 1960).
fieldNotes.truckGate: Wide gated truck entrance on the SW frontage road (~30.0316,-89.9135): a fence opening with sliding/swing gate panels set back from the road and an overhead gantry sign structure spanning the driveway. Clear controlled checkpoint.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No distinct staffed guard booth resolved at the gate in Street View or satellite; a small structure sits near the gate apron but its function is ambiguous. Low confidence, treated as remote check-in (kiosk/call-box).
fieldNotes.remoteGs: Set true because a controlled truck gate is present but no clear guard shack, implies kiosk / call-box check-in. Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Dock activity is split across more than one building face (south face dock apron near 30.0328,-89.9116 and a separate SE dock band near 30.0331,-89.9109); green coffee receiving and finished-goods shipping are physically distinct per site operations.
fieldNotes.railServed: Rail spur runs along the north edge of the property; web research confirms finished coffee ships by rail, truck and water.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Large multi-building campus: main roasting/packaging building, separate processing/silo structures to the NE, and ancillary buildings, more than one large cluster behind the fence.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Gate driveway is wide with substantial unused paved apron width; room exists to add a bypass/express lane.
fieldNotes.dockDoorCount: ~30 estimate from overhead imagery; many bays partially obscured by building shadow and tree cover along faces. Flagged low confidence.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: 73.8 acres for the full fenced manufacturing complex (building cluster plus rail-served processing yard and dock aprons). Historical 1960 footprint was ~20 acres; the operation has expanded substantially.

citations.claim: Smucker self-attests three New Orleans coffee facilities incl. one of the world's largest roasting facilities (Folgers/Dunkin'/Cafe Bustelo), ~700 employees.
Folgers (a Smucker brand) has roasted coffee in New Orleans since 1960; current roasting ops.

verification.rationale: Smucker/Folgers Tier-1 pages confirm current self-operated New Orleans coffee roasting; no closure/sale found.

sites.name: Coffee Silo Operations - New Orleans LA
sites.type: Distribution/Processing - Green coffee bean silo operations
sites.archetypeName: Gate + GS (not BU sens.) + fast lane opp
sites.dossierExcerpt:
The roster pin (29.914282, -90.114356, ROOFTOP) landed inside container stacks
of the Port of New Orleans Napoleon Avenue Container Terminal, not on the
Silocaf building itself. Web research established that Silocaf ("the world's
largest automated silo plant for green-coffee processing") was built in the
early 1990s on the cleared site of the former Public Grain Elevator, at 5240
Coffee Dr inside the port terminal.

Searching the satellite imagery for the distinctive silo cluster located the
facility ~190 m SE of the pin: a compact vertical industrial building with a
visible row of cylindrical bulk-storage silos along its south edge,
processing conveyors, and a blue-roofed annex. This matches a green-coffee silo
plant and is the correct building. Locked center: 29.9139, -90.1122.

fieldNotes.location: Silocaf / Smucker Coffee Silo Operations, the world's largest automated green-coffee silo plant, 5240-5242 Coffee Dr. Built ~1992 on the cleared site of the former Public Grain Elevator. Confirmed via satellite: a compact vertical processing building with a row of cylindrical bulk-storage silos along its south edge, conveyors and a blue-roofed annex, sitting inside the Port of New Orleans Napoleon Avenue Container Terminal.
fieldNotes.truckGate: TRUE but indirect, the Silocaf building has no separate fenced perimeter or its own gate. It sits deep inside the secured Port of New Orleans Napoleon Avenue Container Terminal; all truck access is controlled at the port terminal's manned gate. Classified as a controlled (gated) truck entrance at the terminal level. Flagged uncertain because the gate is the port's, not the facility's own.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Marked true, Port of New Orleans container terminals operate manned gatehouses with TWIC/credential checks. Not directly visible in usable imagery (no public Street View inside the secured terminal); inferred from standard port-terminal security practice. Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.multiStep: Set true, a port-terminal context typically involves a first checkpoint at the terminal gate, then a separate check-in/transfer point at the Silocaf building itself for bulk-coffee loading/unloading. Two-stage check-in is characteristic; flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: 0-10, this is a vertical silo plant, not a flat distribution center. Bulk green coffee moves via hopper trailers, conveyors and pneumatic transfer rather than a long rhythm of dock doors. ~6 transfer/dock points estimated. Flagged low confidence.
fieldNotes.dropArea: 0-10, a handful of trailers (~8 visible, bulk hopper + box) parked on the west apron; no large marked drop-yard. Capacity ~14.
fieldNotes.railServed: TRUE, extensive Public Belt / port rail yards run immediately along the north edge; green coffee is moved by rail as well as truck and ship.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Large open paved terminal aprons surround the facility; ample room exists to organize bypass/express lanes for bulk-coffee trucks.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: 6.1 acres for the Silocaf building footprint plus its immediate truck apron and silo row. The broader Napoleon Avenue Container Terminal it sits within is far larger but is a separate port property.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: 2, the main processing/silo building and an adjacent office/ancillary building to the NE.
fieldNotes.confidence: Medium overall, the facility was positively identified and the silo plant is unambiguous, but it is enclosed within a secured port terminal with no public Street View, so gate/guard-shack/lane details are inferred from port-operations context rather than directly observed.

citations.claim: Smucker self-attests 'our three New Orleans facilities' include the largest bulk coffee facility in the world and references 'our Silo facility'.
Listing for 'Smucker Coffee Silo Operations' at 5242 Coffee Dr handling raw green/decaf/soluble coffee through blending and shipment to roasting.

verification.rationale: Despite legacy 'Silocaf/Pacorini' name, current evidence (Smucker Coffee Silo Operations LLC + Smucker green-coffee-ops staffing) shows Smucker-operated today.

fieldNotes.location: J.M. fieldNotes.dockDoors: 50+, extensive dock banks along the SW/west building face with ~22 trailers visible backed in or parked; a building of ~1,000,000 sq ft footprint of this type carries well over 50 doors. ~55 estimate; flagged low confidence.
fieldNotes.dropArea: 25-50, a dedicated trailer-parking/drop lot adjacent to the SW dock apron; ~22 trailers visible, capacity ~70 across the apron + drop lot.

fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide divided entrance apron with separated in/out lanes and substantial unused paved width; clear room to add a bypass/express lane.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Paved holding area inside the gate before the dock aprons.
fieldNotes.railServed: FALSE, Norfolk Southern rail borders the JeffMet park to the SE, but no rail spur runs into the Smucker plant property itself; the plant ships by truck.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Rural, McCalla is an edge-of-metro small community; the plant sits in an industrial park surrounded by woodland and farmland off US-11, ~24 miles from Birmingham.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: 1, a single very large integrated manufacturing/distribution building.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: 90.1 acres for the developed/fenced operational footprint (building + truck yards + drop lot + employee parking + retention). The full Smucker parcel is ~225 acres.

citations.claim: Smucker celebrated opening of its new ~900k sq ft Uncrustables plant in McCalla AL.
Official Smucker PR confirming McCalla AL Uncrustables plant opening, 3rd dedicated location.

verification.rationale: Smucker's own PR confirms Nov 2024 opening of its $1.1B self-built 3rd Uncrustables plant; operating, not under construction.
